title: Support `<selectedcontent>` in `<select multiple>`
body: This PR adds support for the selectedcontent element in a select element with the multiple attribute. Every option in the select's list of options is cloned into selectedcontent, and each clone has the same selectedness as the option it was cloned from. A new UA style rule hides the clones which aren't selected: ```css select[multiple] selectedcontent > option:not(:checked) { display: none; } ``` Here is what the markup would look like after the selectedcontent element performs its cloning: ```html ``` The clones are not options of the select: selectedcontent now ends the search for an option's nearest ancestor select, and the list of options skips selectedcontent descendants. This also changes select without the multiple attribute, so that an option inside a selectedcontent is no longer one of its options. The UA style rules which give options their size, spacing, layout, and interactive styles exclude the clones with `:not(selectedcontent option)`. Only selectedness is kept in sync. Changing an option's selectedness updates the selectedness of its existing clones without cloning again. Changes to an option's attributes or children are not reflected until the options are cloned again. Each clone keeps its option's `id`, so `getElementById()`, selectors, and ID references can find the clone. The timing matches select without the multiple attribute wherever cloning cost allows: - **Inserting a selectedcontent** (including when its select gets connected) clones the options synchronously in its post-connection steps. - **Adding the multiple attribute** clones the options synchronously, the same way that removing it synchronously updates selectedcontent. - **Inserting, removing, or moving an option** clones the options in a microtask which is coalesced per select. Unlike select without the multiple attribute, the option post-connection steps don't perform the update, so building a select imperatively doesn't clone every option each time one is inserted. Moving an ancestor of the select doesn't clone again. - **While the select is being parsed**, nothing is cloned and no microtasks are queued. The options are cloned once, when the parser finishes parsing the select's children. Microtask timing relative to parsing is inconsistent, which would make the clone timing and mutation records inconsistent. As with select without the multiple attribute, this works the same way whether or not the select is connected.
